.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 631 AM EDT Thursday...

1. Widespread rain is expected to taper off this morning with 
gusty winds from the west anticipated throughout the day. A drier, 
seasonable period is anticipated to end the week as gusty winds 
decrease toward the weekend.

2. A shortwave and cold front will likely pass through the 
region Sunday. Breezy periods, milder temperatures, and some showers 
are expected with no significant hazards anticipated.

3. The highest probability (45%-65%) of rain showers in the 
extended period will be on Tuesday, but no significant impacts 
expected.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 631 AM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Our dynamic weather system will slide east this morning 
with drier low level conditions mixing in from the north and west 
resulting in quickly clearing skies. Temperatures today will be 
warmer than yesterday with highs in the upper 60s and 70s. Winds 
will become gusty once again this afternoon with good vertical 
mixing associated with a lagging low level jet and drying low levels 
behind the departing system. Winds will gust between 20-30 MPH out 
of the west and northwest, locally higher on summits. Winds will 
trend weaker this evening with lighter northwest cold air advection 
by Friday under building high pressure. Depending on how quickly 
winds slacken this evening, some patchy fog, mainly in the 
Adirondacks, and perhaps the St. Lawrence Valley, will be possible 
as skies clear overnight from northwest to southeast. This will also 
be dependent on the timing of a trough crossing the area from north 
to south that could bring an isolated shower or two early on in the 
night. Southeastern Vermont will likely lag behind in the clearing 
department with clouds lingering towards sunrise Friday. Thursday 
night lows will dip into the upper 40s for most of the region, 
outside of areas near Lake Champlain and in the Connecticut River 
Valley, which should have lows around 50 F. The Adirondacks have the 
best opportunity to radiate warmth out with some pocket mid and 
upper 30s in the typical coldest hollows. High pressure will 
dominate through Saturday, resulting in seasonable, dry days and 
cool nights with the potential for valley fog.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A shortwave passing through southern New England may 
bring some light rain to southern portions of our forecast area on 
Sunday morning (20-50% rainfall chances), then a low pressure system 
centered over Hudson Bay will drag a cold frontal boundary through 
the region throughout the day Sunday, with highest chances for 
rainfall along the international border (50-80% Sunday afternoon). 
Temperatures Saturday night will be on the milder side with lows in 
the 50s and lower 60s, then Sunday's highs will be dependent on 
showers but generally on the warmer side in southerly/southwesterly 
flow with highs in the 70s and lower 80s.

KEY MESSAGE 3: A progressive west to east pattern is progged to be acrs 
our cwa for days 4 thru 7, supporting a boundary every couple of 
days with near normal temps. The deepest moisture and best 
instability looks to be mostly south of our cwa, but pw values 1.60-
1.90" ahead of boundary on Tuesday with some weak instability wl 
produce a band of showers, similar to what we experienced on Weds 
evening. Given sfc based CAPE values btwn 250-400 J/kg, the 
probability of severe is <10% attm. The llvl gradient strengthens 
ahead of approaching cold frnt with progged 850mb winds of 30 to 45 
knots, supporting localized gusts 25 to 40 mph, especially summits 
and Lake Champlain. Progged 925mb temps warm btwn 17-20C Tues/Weds, 
supporting highs well into the 70s with a few lower 80s possible in 
the warmer valleys if some sunshine develops on southwest downslope 
flow. A deeper/sharper mid/upper lvl trof and associated low pres is 
progged to develop acrs the Mid Atlantic/SNE Coast by late next 
week. Still plenty of uncertainty on placement/track of sfc low pres 
and if any moisture can spread this farther north. For now WPC has 
some chc pops on Thurs. Temps cool back into the mid 60s to mid 70s 
for Weds/Thurs with lows near 40F SLK to lower/mid 50s near Lake 
Champlain for midweek.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Through 12Z Friday...Currently a mix of MVFR and VFR conditions
across our taf sites this morning. Expecting any lingering MVFR
cigs at PBG/SLK and EFK to lift by 14z and covered this idea
with a two hour tempo. As mixing increases this morning expect
southwest winds 10 to 15 knots with gusts 15 to 25 knots to
develop by 15z and slowly change to the west/northwest as a
secondary cold front drops across our taf sites. By this evening
additional mid level clouds and a few sprinkles are possible as
boundary layer mixing continues. These factors should limit the
areal coverage of fog and IFR or lower conditions, but SLK/MPV
and EFK will need to be watched, given recent rainfall.

Outlook...

Friday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Friday Night: VFR. Patchy BR.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance
SHRA.
Sunday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA, Slight
chance TSRA.
Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Monday: VFR. NO SIG WX.

&&

.MARINE...
Southwesterly wind gusts 10 to 15 knots are expected on Lake 
Champlain this morning, becoming northwesterly 15 to 20 knots
with gusts around 25 knots this afternoon. Waves will be around
1 to 3 feet today. Winds will become weaker tonight around 5 to
15 knots out of the northwest.
